answer: In an oasis marketplace where agents trade plume forecasts and jade appraisals, each trading identity must lock a $100 bond for 90 days before it can accept orders. Escrow caps each identity’s unsettled orders at its bond value, and verified nondelivery forfeits the bond to buyers. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000; abandoning them after taking orders burns the collateral instead of making new identities a cheap reset.
